messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR senior brief: flight-check and contingency catalog

Team —

As we prep the QBR pack, I want a concise senior-level brief that: (1) states current roadmap status across Product & Eng, (2) highlights launch timelines we still expect to meet vs at-risk, and (3) contains a short contingency catalog (what we’d do at T-7, T-3, T-0 relative to launch).

Key asks for this thread: please reply with the short status bullets for your area by EOD Wed (04/07). I attached a quick workbook with a suggested layout (qbr_flight_checks.xlsx).

What I care about for the deck: clear RAG for each launch lane, single-line impact statement for customer-facing risk, and a proposed mitigation (owner + time to implement). Keep it executive-friendly — we will have 12 minutes in the QBR for this section.

Notes / constraints:
- We have two launches in scope: NimbusPay integration (major customer, GA target 06/01) and Model-Optimize rollout (internal; target 05/15 infra-wide).
- Primary risk vectors: infra autoscaling (esp. long-tail traffic), model quality regressions on large-context sequences, and rollout windows that overlap product marketing activities.

Irene — would like your engineering read (short bullets) capturing technical risk and any expected schedule movement.

Thanks,
Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product & Strategy, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR senior brief: flight-check and contingency catalog

Vivek —

Quick engineering read below (short bullets as requested). I also exported a short risk table into the Drive file: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1QBRFlightChecks (see tab \"ENG-RISKS\").

NimbusPay integration (GA 2027-06-01) — AT RISK
- Why: integration requires a per-customer routing policy and reserved-capacity pinning that is not yet in the Dedicated infra API (infra feature gap).
- Impact: if not delivered, we must run Nimbus on shared-hosted with throttled concurrency — risk to latency SLO for their peak traffic windows (even if token cost ok).
- Mitigation (T-7): freeze new feature toggles; run extended canary during their scheduled peak hours. (Owner: Karthik; effort: 2 engineer-days + infra ops runbook).
- Forward action: INF-3421 is open for the routing API; ETA for a minimal MVP is 2027-05-10 (depends on infra PRs).

Model-Optimize rollout (internal, 2027-05-15) — YELLOW
- Why: quantized kernels show nondeterministic perf on sequence lengths >8k in nightly tests. Failures are intermittent but reproducible on specific prompts.
- Impact: potential latency spikes and higher token decode tail latency for a subset of customers.
- Mitigation: restrict large-context routing to q2 only; add fallback to float16 model variant for long sequences (adds cost). (Owner: Irene; effort: 3 engineer-days + perf regression window).

General infra notes:
- Autoscaling: we've tuned horizontal autoscale but need a reactive vertical buffer to handle correlated long-tail bursts. Ops Playbook attached (infra_canary_playbook.pdf).
- Rollout windows: recommend splitting Nimbus GA into a phased window (first half of June reserved for key accounts, public GA mid-June). This reduces blast radius and gives us more observation time.

I will drop a short summary slide into the Drive file (ENG slide). Will also link the Jira tickets.

Irene —

From a CS/Customer Impact lens: short notes to fold into the single-line impact statements:
- NimbusPay: their onboarding timeline is tied to a marketing event and they expect dedicated SLAs. If we push GA, we should offer an interim engineering SLA and a migration playbook + two dedicated support engineers during their ramp.
- Model-Optimize: callout that some enterprise customers use >8k contexts in legal/finance flows — any fallback to float16 must be framed as temporary with a clear plan to restore precision.

Irene — happy to draft the customer-facing language for the QBR slide so execs can see the communications cadence.

—
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: QBR senior brief: flight-check and contingency catalog

Irene / Vivek —

Short mitigation plan for the Nimbus routing gap:
- Technical fix: implement minimal routing API in infra to allow per-customer pinning (INF-3421). Patch should be backward-compatible and expose a toggle for Dedicated vs Shared routing.
- Canary plan: extended canary for Nimbus with synthetic traffic replay during their peak window (details in infra_canary_playbook.pdf).
- Timeline: working prototype by 2027-04-22; code review and infra validation by 2027-05-05; deploy to staging 2027-05-12.
- Risk if delayed: move to phased GA as Irene suggested (first wave = 3 pilot accounts).
